blocks.text: Neurons follow particular neural pathways (arcs) to receive, transmit and process impulses. Some pathways have only a few neurons; others are complex networks. The reflex arc is the simplest neural pathway; it controls reflex actions, immediate, automatic and involuntary responses to external and internal stimuli.

items: A hammer taps the patellar tendon below the knee; the tap is the stimulus.
A receptor in the quadriceps muscle of the thigh senses it and starts an impulse in a sensory neuron.
The sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord and passes it to a motor neuron directly, without an inter-neuron.
The motor neuron carries the impulse to the effector, the quadriceps, which contracts: the lower leg kicks forward at the knee.

Meanwhile the sensory neuron also activates an inter-neuron in the spinal cord, which releases chemicals that inhibit the motor neurons of the hamstrings, so the hamstrings relax while the leg extends.

blocks.alt: Side view of a bent leg. A hammer strikes the tendon below the knee. A sensory neuron runs from a receptor in the quadriceps muscle at the front of the thigh to the spinal cord, shown in cross-section. Inside the cord an interneuron is drawn, and two motor neurons leave the cord, one to the quadriceps and one to the hamstrings muscle at the back of the thigh.
